title: TRUNCATE staging table with no pre-DDL backup
expected_feedback: Critical: TRUNCATE is DDL, not DML. It auto-commits, cannot be rolled back, and resets the high-water mark, so the 4M rows are gone the instant it succeeds. It is also on the list of structural operations that FLASHBACK TABLE ... TO SCN/TIMESTAMP cannot cross, so the usual undo is unavailable — the recovery path is a pre-TRUNCATE copy, a guaranteed restore point, or RMAN PITR, and it must exist before the statement runs. If the intent is merely to empty a staging table between loads that is defensible, but the review must still record the phase as irreversible and confirm the source data can be re-derived.
violated_rule: Irreversible statements need a pre-DDL artefact
